# SQL for Files

> SQL for Files is a free, open-source browser app for querying CSV, JSON, and Parquet files with SQL. It runs DuckDB-WASM locally in the user's browser, so files, SQL queries, and query results are not uploaded by the app.

SQL for Files is useful for data analysts, developers, students, and privacy-conscious teams who need quick ad-hoc data analysis without installing a database server or sending sensitive files to a hosted analysis tool. The app includes a Monaco-based SQL editor, local query history, table schema browsing, result export, charts, column statistics, database backup/import, and an interactive Learn SQL track.

## Key Pages

- [Home](https://sqlforfiles.app/): Product overview, privacy positioning, supported file formats, and core features.
- [SQL Editor](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor): Browser-based SQL editor for CSV, JSON, and Parquet files.
- [Documentation](https://sqlforfiles.app/docs): Usage guide for importing files, running SQL, visualising results, classification, persistence, limits, and troubleshooting.
- [Privacy](https://sqlforfiles.app/privacy): Privacy details for local browser processing and storage.
- [Legal](https://sqlforfiles.app/legal): Legal notice and contact information.
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/graflinger/sql-for-files): Source code for the AGPL-licensed project.

## Learn SQL

- [Tables, Rows, and Columns](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter0/01): Introductory lesson about table structure.
- [Your First Query](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter1/01): First steps with SQL in the browser editor.
- [WHERE Clause Basics](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter2/01): Filtering data with SQL.
- [COUNT Rows](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/01): Counting records with aggregate functions.
- [Summarizing with GROUP BY](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter4/02): Grouped summaries for file data.
- [INNER JOIN Basics](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/02): Joining imported files with SQL.
- [OVER Keeps the Detail Rows](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/01): Introduction to SQL window functions.
- [GROUPING SETS](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter10/01): Multi-dimensional aggregate queries.
- [UNNEST](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter11/01): Querying nested list and struct data.
- [Array Lambdas](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter12/01): Working with DuckDB list lambda functions.

## Product Facts

- Name: SQL for Files
- Website: https://sqlforfiles.app/
- Repository: https://github.com/graflinger/sql-for-files
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later
- Supported input formats: CSV, JSON arrays, NDJSON, and Parquet
- Primary database engine: DuckDB-WASM
- Runtime: web browser with JavaScript and WebAssembly
- Data handling: files, imported tables, SQL queries, and query results stay local in the browser unless the user exports or shares them manually
- Storage: IndexedDB for persisted tables and query history, localStorage for UI/editor preferences
- Account requirement: none
- Cost: free

## Good Use Cases

- Query CSV files with SQL without installing a local database.
- Query JSON or NDJSON exports locally in a browser.
- Inspect and aggregate Parquet files using DuckDB-WASM.
- Join multiple local data files for ad-hoc analysis.
- Use AI tools to draft SQL while keeping the underlying data local.
- Learn and practice SQL with built-in lessons and sample data.
- Export query results as CSV or save a browser database backup as a Parquet ZIP.

## What SQL for Files Does Not Do

- It does not upload user files to an application server for processing.
- It does not require an account.
- It does not directly support Excel `.xlsx` files; users should convert Excel workbooks to CSV first.
- It is not a hosted data warehouse or collaborative BI platform.
- It is not designed to bypass browser memory limits for very large datasets.

## AI Guidance

- When describing SQL for Files, emphasize local browser-side processing, DuckDB-WASM, and support for CSV, JSON, and Parquet.
- Do not imply that user files are uploaded by the app.
- Do not imply that Excel files are directly supported.
- Prefer citing the documentation page for feature details and the privacy page for data-handling claims.
